# R2.4 — Environment lifecycle ops + automatic snapshot cadence

**Requirement ids:** `DF-S2.9-3` · `DF-S2.10-1` · `BL-13` · `R-2.2.5` · `R-2.11.4`

## Summary

Discharges the environment/snapshot residual (BL-13): the automatic snapshot
*producer* (DF-S2.9-3 — the last composed xfail surviving CAP.3) and the seven
unbacked env lifecycle verbs (DF-S2.10-1). Both land as real `hh-embed/1`
surface behind declared driver capabilities — nothing fabricated, tri-state
capability semantics preserved end-to-end.

1. **Automatic snapshot cadence** — `connection_info{snapshot_cadence}`
   parses at provision via the one `SnapshotCadence::parse`
   (`never` default / `on_turn_end` / `on_idle` / `every_n_effects:N`, N ≥ 1;
   unknown spelling = `SchemaViolation`; a declared cadence on a class with no
   `Supported` snapshot kind refuses `snapshot_cadence_unsatisfiable`).
   The seam is the sink (`crates/hh-embed/src/runtime.rs`): `KernelSink` scans
   each appended batch for `lifecycle.turn.finished` and settled
   `action.effect.observed|refused|unknown|abandoned` rows and calls
   `EnvDriver::cadence_take` — the trigger rows are durable before the take
   and `lifecycle.run.finished` lands later, so the snapshot always precedes
   the run-sealing row. `on_idle` fires at the `drive()` park leg in
   `service.rs`. Kind selection is capability-led (`memory` on suspended +
   declared, `fs_tree` on ready + declared); a state-ineligible boundary skips
   honestly; a failed take mints
   `action.environment.failed{op:"snapshot.cadence"}` (audited, never
   run-fatal). Takes stamp `taken_by:"cadence"`/`"suspend"`.
2. **The seven env ops** (`env.open`/`attach`/`close`/`diff`/`restore`/
   `upload`/`download`) — additive `hh-embed/1` members (CC7/CC8; schema export
   + compat matrix + generated client regenerated, drift-clean) dispatched in
   `envops.rs` through the session's bound handle: open = provision+attach+
   `action.environment.selected`+session rebind; `close{mode:"detach"}` is the
   survivable form vs default teardown; `diff` re-walks live roots against a
   named `fs_tree` baseline; `restore` defaults successor
   (`restored`+`replaced`+rebind), `mode:"in_place"` gated on
   `restore_in_place`; upload takes exactly one of `content`/`content_address`
   into a writable root; download returns the `ContentAddress` (bytes never
   cross the boundary). Both transfer directions mint the new audit rows
   `action.environment.uploaded`/`downloaded`. Provider-class handles refuse
   the fs surface as `UnknownCapability` — typed refusals, never fake success;
   R-NOSIDE holds (no `EnvHandleId` in results).
3. **Hibernate + restore_in_place verified** — `suspend{on_idle:"hibernate"}`
   mints the memory snapshot in the same durable batch
   (`taken_by:"suspend"`, threaded into
   `action.environment.suspended{hibernation_snapshot}`);
   `restore{mode:"in_place"}` exercises the declared `restore_in_place`
   capability; `local_host` answers the honest `UnknownCapability`.
4. **CLI + roots** — all seven `hh env` verbs dispatch through the boundary
   (ledger effect byte-identical, K-1); the `stage_pending` catch-all covers
   only genuinely unrouted verbs. `Roots::is_writable`/`is_readable`
   canonicalize both operands (`canonicalize_path` — deepest-existing-ancestor
   symlink resolution), fixing the macOS `/var`→`/private/var` lexical
   mismatch without weakening escape refusal.

## Decisions

ADR-0335: the cadence seam at the sink (vs the turn loop — ordering is
structural), fail-closed cadence parsing at provision, capability-led kind
selection with audited misses, the `env.*` vocabulary kept (per the ticket
note), canonicalized root checks, and the new refusal-cited capability keys
(`fs.upload`, `fs.download`, `restore.successor`, `attach.backend`).
